<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope consists entirely of variable assignments, array definitions, and function definitions. When `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources the PKGBUILD, it only executes code in the global top-level scope and does NOT run `pkgver()`, `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` functions. 

The top-level code includes assignments for `pkgbase`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `DLAGENTS`, `source`, and `sha256sums`, plus the `_install_font()` function definition and the `package_*()` function declarations. Function definitions in bash do not execute their bodies merely by being defined — the bodies only run when the function is explicitly called, and `--printsrcinfo` does not call any package functions.

The `DLAGENTS` entry references `curl` for HTTPS downloads, but since `--printsrcinfo` does not download or verify sources at all, this definition does not trigger any network execution. The `source` URL (`https://www.kreativekorp.com/swdownload/fonts/retro/lisa1.zip`) points to the official upstream site, and the `sha256sums` entry contains a checksum value — both are standard packaging practices. No top-level command substitutions, `eval`, `base64`, `curl|bash`, or other dangerous patterns are present. There are no data exfiltration attempts, reverse shells, or unexpected system modifications at the global scope.

Because no genuinely malicious code executes during the sourcing/parsing step, this gate passes as SAFE.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>No dangerous top-level code executes during makepkg --printsrcinfo</summary>
